_meta.source: Statistics South Africa — Consumer Price Index (P0141); SARB Monetary Policy Committee
_meta.update_frequency: Monthly — around the 22nd of each month for the prior month
_meta.notes: CPI figures are year-on-year % change (all urban areas, headline). Latest Stats SA CPI release: September 2026 (published 2026-10-21; added in an addendum on 2026-10-22, after the 2026-10-19 research cutoff). Headline 4.5% (Aug 4.4%, Jul 4.3%); food & NAB 1.2% (Aug 1.1%, Jul 0.9%) per Stats SA's release article https://www.statssa.gov.za/?p=20031 (the statistical release PDF was not retrieved). A third-party agricultural commentary quoted a different food figure (1.0%) and was disregarded in favour of Stats SA's own 1.2%. Next CPI (October 2026) is due 2026-11-18. SARB inflation target is 3% with a ±1 percentage point tolerance band (SARB MPC page, September 2026); the 12 Nov 2025 adoption date quoted in earlier notes was not re-verified. 2026 repo decisions verified: held 6.75% (29 Jan, 26 Mar); raised to 7.00% (28 May, effective 29 May, 4–2 vote); held 7.00% (23 Jul, 4–2); raised to 7.25% (23 Sep, effective 25 Sep, unanimous). Months May–Sep 2026 were added from Stats SA P0141 releases (May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep 2026). REVIEW: monthly points before Apr 2026 were not re-verified; the stored food series shows a rise Jan→Feb 2026 (3.5→3.7), which conflicts with Stats SA's statement of an eight-month downswing to July 2026; annual-cpi-avg (2025 = 3.2%) was not re-verified. Duplicate of repo-rate-sarb in interest-rates.json is retained (both 7.25%). Do NOT run the World Bank updater script for this dataset (it overwrites verified values with annual modelled figures); update manually from the official Stats SA/SARB/DBE release — see antigravity-instructions.md. REVIEW: repo-rate series points 'Jul 2025' (7.25%) and 'Jan 2025' (7.75%) look one meeting out of date versus media reports of a cut to 7.00% on 2025-07-31; retained unchanged pending SARB statement check. New points follow the convention 'rate in force after that month's MPC decision'.

_meta.public_notes: CPI figures are year-on-year percentage changes (headline, all urban areas). Latest Stats SA CPI release: September 2026 (published 21 October 2026). The SARB inflation target is 3%, with a tolerance band of 1 percentage point either side. Each repo-rate point is the rate in force after that month's Monetary Policy Committee decision. Monthly points before April 2026 have not yet been rechecked against the original releases.

statistics.title: Headline Inflation (CPI)
statistics.description: South Africa's headline CPI was 4.5% year-on-year in September 2026, up from 4.4% in August and 4.3% in July; the index rose 0.4% between August and September. Inflation peaked at 5.0% in June, the highest since June 2024. Transport (10.8%, contributing 1.5 percentage points), housing and utilities (5.2%, 1.3 points) and insurance and financial services (5.4%, 0.6 points) were the main contributors. The SARB's inflation target is 3% with a tolerance band of ±1 percentage point.

statistics.title: Food & Non-Alcoholic Beverages CPI
statistics.description: Food and non-alcoholic beverage (NAB) inflation was 1.2% in September 2026, up from 1.1% in August and 0.9% in July, a second consecutive monthly increase. Meat inflation slowed to 0.7% (its lowest since March 2025) and cereal products recorded an eighth consecutive month of deflation (-1.9%).

statistics.title: SARB Policy Rate (Repo Rate)
statistics.description: The SARB raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 7.25% at its 23 September 2026 MPC meeting (effective 25 September). The decision was unanimous, and was the second increase of 2026 after a hike to 7.00% in May; the committee held at 7.00% in July. The MPC cited a persistent global energy-price shock, elevated services inflation and upside inflation risks. The prime lending rate is now 10.75%. The SARB's inflation target is 3% with a tolerance band of ±1 percentage point.

statistics.title: Annual Average CPI (Full Year)
statistics.description: South Africa's full-year average headline CPI for 2025 was 3.2%, the lowest annual average in 21 years, confirmed by Stats SA in January 2026. The annual average was 6.9% in 2022.
